about: Claims of the Thinking length investigation (TL-*) and of the CuteAFD v5 context probe (CP-*), generated from the results by tools/build_findings.py. Each evidence entry names a repository file and an RFC 6901 JSON pointer; 'value' is what the pointer resolved to at build time. tools/verify.py re-resolves every pointer and recomputes entries that carry 'recompute' from the per-reply tables (CP-bf16-distance: from the per-window figures).

status_vocabulary.measurement: frozen rule: protocol and decision rule frozen (hashes in the run's protocol/FROZEN.json) before the first request
status_vocabulary.measurement: post hoc: computed from frozen-run data after the run; not part of any decision rule
status_vocabulary.measurement: descriptive: counted from frozen-run data; not part of any decision rule
status_vocabulary.exploratory: run kind exploratory: useful evidence, not a frozen comparison
status_vocabulary.source reading: read in source code and logs, no measurement
status_vocabulary.judgement: source and measurements: a conclusion drawn from source reading and published measurements together; not isolated by a run of its own
status_vocabulary.measurement: extension: passes added by a dated amendment, written after the frozen result was read and before the first added request; the frozen rule applied to more passes; not the frozen comparison
status_vocabulary.measurement: planned descriptive: plan and file hashes written before the first request of the stage, after earlier results were read; descriptive, with no gate and no decision rule
status_vocabulary.accounting: checkpoint files: counted from the headers of the checkpoint files; no model is run and nothing is compared by a rule

conventions.interval: 95% bootstrap over the unit in ci_over (percentile); 4,000 draws for TL-* entries, 10,000 for CP-* entries; TL-* seeds are in each run's protocol; CP-* entries use seed 5 with percentile indices 250 and 9749 (frozen rule, and the post hoc share-of-unfinished intervals of CP-fourpass-endings), and seed 7 or 20261111 with indices 250 and 9750 (post hoc and by-family readings), stated per entry in recompute.bootstrap and in analysis/posthoc.py; CP-bf16-* entries use window bootstraps (fidelity set: 5,000 replicates, SplitMix64 seed 20260829, linear-interpolation percentiles; teacher panel: 20,000 replicates, numpy generator seed 20260929)
conventions.detected: interval excludes the null (1 for ratios, 0 for differences)
conventions.pointers: RFC 6901: split on '/', then replace '~1' with '/' and '~0' with '~' (keys such as 'C-K6x/V-BF16' contain a slash)

definitions.finished: finish_reason == 'stop' and hit_cap == False (a reply that ended on its own under the 130,048-token cap)
definitions.reasoning_tokens: tokens of the reasoning text, by re-tokenizing it with the model's tokenizer
definitions.seed_paired_ratio: for each (prompt, rep) where both arms finished: log(reasoning tokens A / B); ratio = exp(mean over all such pairs); interval: bootstrap over prompts (resample prompts with replacement, pool their pairs)
definitions.bootstrap_draws: rng = random.Random(seed); each draw: rng.choice(sorted prompt list) repeated once per prompt, mean of the pooled log ratios; sort the 4,000 draw means; interval = exp of values at indices 100 and 3899
definitions.cross_engine_ratio: post hoc: for each (prompt, rep) where both finished: log(A / B); mean within each prompt; mean over prompts; exp. Each prompt weighs the same, so a same-engine contrast differs slightly from seed_paired_ratio
definitions.pass_pairs: post hoc: for each (prompt, rep) where both arms finished: all_tests_pass A minus B (1, 0 or -1); mean over the pairs; interval: bootstrap over prompts as bootstrap_draws, on the pooled differences (seed 20261108)
definitions.engine_comparison: vLLM ratio / CuteAFD ratio = exp(mean over prompts of [vLLM prompt log ratio - CuteAFD prompt log ratio])

context_probe.applies_to: CP-* entries (results/2026-11-10-context-probe); the definitions above apply to TL-* entries
context_probe.rows_used: analysis/samples.csv rows with final == 1 and status == ok (one per request; delivery turns of the eight-turn pass have final == 0); for the reference checkpoint, the same rows of analysis/samples-reference.csv beside them; for passes 3 and 4 (CP-fourpass-*), the same rows of analysis/samples-extension.csv beside both
context_probe.request_score: correct / fields if finish_class == 'stop' and fields > 0, else 0 (a reply that hit the cap or was ended by the loop abort scores 0)
context_probe.item_paired_difference_frozen: for each item, over the (pass, length) cells in recompute.passes x recompute.lengths where both arms have a row: request_score(b) - request_score(a); mean within the item (statistics.fmean); estimate = mean over items, rounded to 4 places. Interval: items in sorted order, rng = random.Random(5); 10,000 draws, each the fmean of n values vals[rng.randrange(n)]; sorted draws at indices 250 and 9749
context_probe.item_paired_difference_pooled: post hoc: items of recompute.family (all items if absent), sorted; per item and arm, the mean over passes x lengths of request_score (or of every_field_right when strict); d = b - a per item; estimate = sum(d) / n. Interval: rng = random.Random(seed); 10,000 draws, each sum of n values d[rng.randrange(n)] / n; sorted draws at indices 250 and 9750
context_probe.item_paired_unfinished_share: post hoc (CP-fourpass-endings; recompute.value == 'unfinished'): as item_paired_difference_frozen with 1 if finish_class != 'stop' else 0 in place of request_score, over the items of recompute.family, so the per-item value is the share of the item's replies in the cell that did not finish, b - a; same generator, seed and indices
context_probe.sign: 'b - a': above 0 = arm b scored higher (for item_paired_unfinished_share: arm b left more replies unfinished)

findings.question: What differs between CuteAFD's two core formats besides the core's weights?
findings.answer: With a BF16 core, CuteAFD v4.0.0's launcher also puts the KDA projections (including three gate projections outside the core) and the vocabulary head in FP8, and prefill runs the MLA and MLP projections with FP8 activations; with the native 6-bit core these stay on the 6-bit kernels or in BF16. On a two-GPU head split the FP8 KDA path also comes with KDA output sharding, which v4 accepts only with FP8 KDA and clears for the native core. These are the launcher's defaults (its comment at run-family.sh:2337-2351, v4.0.0), with the author's stated reasons: decode speed and pool size, and output sharding to avoid rounding the GPUs' partial outputs, checked on teacher-forced top-1 and KL. The model notes (docs/models/glm5_flash.md 'Default precision') and the --kda-fp8 option text (mod.rs:189-197) describe BF16 KDA as the two-GPU default; the documents differ, and the launcher's choice is what runs.

findings.question: Which part of CuteAFD's FP8 path goes with the shorter code reasoning of the BF16-core checkpoint (local derived checkpoint, not a producer release)?

Settings were switched off cumulatively.

findings.question: Where in CuteAFD does the code-length difference arise: prefill or generation?
findings.answer: Most likely on the generation path (decode and speculative verify); prefill is not excluded. Prompts are 1,155-1,758 tokens against medians of 50-68K reasoning tokens; speculative verify steps run on the decode programs, which read the FP8 KDA copies, and KDA output sharding is not limited to prefill. The KDA setting also changes the KDA projections in prefill, and the prompt's recurrent state seeds every later token. Not separated: KDA in prefill against generation, plain decode against speculative verify.

findings.answer: It falls in every arm, the BF16 reference included: field score 0.98 at 4K and 0.89 to 0.91 at 127K. findings.question: Did the eight-turn pass test a conversation whose history the model wrote?
findings.answer: No. Decode ran in every reply, but the model's own turns were a median 9% of the final prompt at 4K and 0.3-0.4% at 127K: at long context over 99% of the history was written by prefill. What the pass shows is split delivery: delivering the same input as eight messages shows no accuracy cost (16K to 127K: every interval includes 0, a cost up to about 0.07 is not excluded; 4K: eight turns score slightly higher in anchor and hqa, intervals exclude 0). The turn design is to be revised.

findings.question: Over four single-message passes, does the K6 core (ATTENTION_MODE=compact) cost accuracy, and where?
findings.answer: Indicated, not established. compact is the lowest arm in both pass sets (four lengths, four passes: 0.946 against 0.955 to 0.959), and the gap is at 127K: 0.887 against 0.918 to 0.924; up to 64K it is level with the others. hqa - compact: +0.037 [+0.004, +0.073] at 127K and +0.013 [+0.002, +0.024] over four lengths (both exclude 0; over four lengths the interval excludes 0 only at four passes, in neither pass set alone). compact - anchor: -0.031 [-0.070, +0.008] at 127K and -0.010 [-0.021, +0.002] over four lengths (both include 0), so hqa and compact separate from each other while neither separates from anchor. Basis of the strength: the same sign in both pass sets and, at 127K, in every pass against hqa (hqa 0.929, 0.896, 0.927, 0.946; compact 0.885, 0.894, 0.892, 0.877) and in three of four against anchor (0.875, 0.931, 0.923, 0.942; pass 1 reverses); not one interval among 102, of which 6 exclude 0 at four passes where about 5 would with no difference anywhere. These counts alone do not settle where the gap comes from. Pooled over four passes it matches the unfinished replies (14 of 240 at 127K against 7, 5, 4; finished replies score 0.942 against 0.936 to 0.945), but the two pass sets do not agree on that split: in passes 1-2 compact had as many unfinished replies at 127K as anchor (5 and 5) and a lower finished-only score (0.928 against 0.942); in passes 3-4 it had 9 unfinished against 2, 2, 3 and the highest finished-only score (0.956). Of its 18 unfinished replies over all lengths, 15 reached the reply cap and 3 ended on the repetition abort. A scoring capture on given texts to 128K, which samples nothing, shows no deficit for compact at predicting text (NLL minus anchor's -0.0055 [-0.0109, -0.0004], lower is better; exploratory, one capture). The capture scores given text and does not locate the gap, which was seen in generated replies at 127K. The 127K length lies beyond the 14.4K reach of both BF16 reference sets, so the BF16 stage (CP-bf16-distance) neither supports nor contradicts this. Added 2026-11-12, after this entry was first published: the replies themselves were read (CP-fourpass-endings). The gap is join replies at 127K that did not finish, not answers that were wrong; whether the K6 projections raise the rate of that ending is indicated, not established.

findings.question: How far are the four configurations from the unquantized BF16 model, and how much of that distance lies in what differs between the probe arms?
findings.answer: All four sit in one band. Fidelity set (coarse KL from BF16, generated positions, contexts to 14.4K): hqa 0.0302 [0.0255, 0.0344], compact 0.0314 [0.0263, 0.0359], anchor 0.0328 [0.0275, 0.0377], exlr8-k4 0.0360 [0.0300, 0.0416]; that is 1.4 to 1.7 times the baseline the engine author recorded in the fidelity set's manifest for the official FP8 model (0.0216; quoted, not recomputed here) and 0.62 to 0.74 of a K3.25 Core-FP8 checkpoint measured on CuteAFD v3.0.1 on 2026-10-26 (0.0484; teacher panel 0.0476); both are rows from other measurements, for scale. Teacher panel (full-vocabulary KL, 2K contexts): anchor 0.0320 [0.0241, 0.0419], hqa 0.0316 [0.0238, 0.0410], compact 0.0297 [0.0236, 0.0364], exlr8-k4 0.0305 [0.0244, 0.0374]. The two sets use different measures and are not comparable with each other. What differs between the three probe arms is a small part of the distance: they share their K4 experts and differ by at most 0.0026 on the fidelity set, under a tenth of the total. The plan stated in advance that anchor's distance would not be zero (quantized experts and the engine's numerics; the two are not separated here). anchor is also not the closest: hqa - anchor is -0.0026 [-0.0042, -0.0011] on the fidelity set (interval excludes 0; hqa closer) and -0.0004 [-0.0014, +0.0006] on the teacher panel (includes 0). anchor differs from hqa in its output head as well as its core (both BF16 in anchor, which is launched with the engine's three FP8 conversion settings off; as logged, KDA FP8 reads Off in every serving launch of the three probe arms and the FP8 prefill setting reads none in anchor and [Mla, Ffn] in hqa and compact) and is a locally derived checkpoint; why it measures slightly farther than hqa on one set is an open question (added 2026-11-12). exlr8-k4 is 0.003 to 0.006 farther than each probe arm on the fidelity set (intervals exclude 0) and level with them on the teacher panel. The two sets place it differently and this stage does not say which is nearer. The fidelity set is the engine author's; its relation to the calibration data of either checkpoint is not known. The teacher panel is drawn from the corpus the producer of the K4 experts published and can favour the experts the three probe arms carry (stated in the plan before the first request); a tilt of that kind would run toward the probe arms. exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component. 30 intervals are listed (24 fidelity set, 6 teacher panel), 13 exclude 0, all on the fidelity set; none was selected. Neither set reaches past 14.4K: the 64K and 127K lengths of the task runs have no BF16 reference here, so the one task difference indicated in this run (CP-fourpass-compact-127k) lies beyond both sets. Basis: one launch per arm plus an exact repeat (CP-bf16-repeat), two reference sets. Limits: one engine build, one checkpoint revision per arm, prefill path only, contexts to 14.4K; descriptive, with no gate and no ranking rule, and the two sets do not order the four configurations the same way.

findings.question: How did the replies of the four single-message passes end, and what is compact's lower score at 127K made of?
findings.answer: 44 of 3,840 replies did not finish (anchor 9, hqa 9, compact 18, exlr8-k4 8), none of them with answer text, so each scores 0 under the frozen rule whatever its reasoning had reached. compact's excess is in one place, the join family at 127K: 10 of 80 replies unfinished against anchor 4, hqa 2, exlr8-k4 1; every unfinished join reply of the run is at 127K. ledger is level (anchor 5, hqa 7, compact 7, exlr8-k4 7 over all lengths) and trace has 1 in total. The 127K difference in score is that family: hqa - compact +0.037, of which join +0.035; anchor - compact +0.031, of which join +0.027. The finished join replies at 127K score level (0.989 to 0.997 over the four configurations). The ending is one every configuration shows, the BF16-core anchor included: in 15 of the 17 unfinished join replies at least half of the reasoning is the prompt's records copied out in order, and in the 16 of them with a copy run all eight of the item's correct identifiers (13 replies) or seven of them (3) occur in the reasoning before the run starts (a text match). Whether the K6 q_b_proj and o_proj raise the rate of that ending is indicated, not established: the paired difference in the share of unfinished join replies at 127K is +0.100 [+0.025, +0.175] for compact - hqa (excludes 0) and +0.075 [-0.013, +0.163] for compact - anchor (includes 0), and by pass compact had 1, 2, 4, 3 and anchor 3, 1, 0, 0, so passes 1-2 alone show no excess. Read with CP-fourpass-compact-127k: the gap there is replies that did not finish, not answers that were wrong. Not measured: a larger reply cap, other sampling settings, a limit on reasoning length, natural documents. Limits: post hoc; 20 items per family; the thresholds for copying (share of at least 0.5) and for a copy run (20 lines) were chosen after the replies were seen (the 44 unfinished replies are listed with their shares, so another threshold can be applied); reply text is not published, only the derived per-reply counts.

findings.note: Definitions and estimators. Unfinished: finish class other than stop (the reply reached the 32,768-token reply cap, or the engine's repetition abort ended it). Step line: a line of the reasoning that carries the record following, in the prompt, the record of the previous such line. Copy share: characters on step lines / characters of the reasoning; copying: copy share of at least 0.5. Copy run: 20 or more consecutive step lines. Share of unfinished replies: per item, the share of its replies in the cell that did not finish; the difference b - a is taken per item (20 join items) and the 95% interval is the 2.5th and 97.5th percentile (sorted-draw indices 250 and 9,749) of 10,000 item resamples, Python random.Random(5). Difference in score by family: each family's mean request score x its share of the requests (one third), so the families sum to the difference over all families up to rounding. Post hoc: SUMMARY.json lists 60 such share intervals (5 pairs, 3 pass sets, 4 cells), of which 9 exclude 0, on top of the intervals of the four-pass tables; none was selected by a rule and no correction is applied. The data are the frozen run's two passes and the two added by amendment 1. analysis/endings.py recomputes analysis/ENDINGS.json from the three per-request tables and analysis/endings.csv; the per-reply counts in endings.csv were derived from reply text that is not published, so they cannot be re-derived from this repository.

findings.question: In one unit, how large is each configuration's checkpoint compared with the unquantized BF16 model, and where do the configurations differ?
findings.answer: Bits per weight (stored bits / weights; BF16 = 16), language model as stored: anchor 4.35 (27.2% of BF16, 162.3 GiB); hqa 4.17 (26.1% of BF16, 155.8 GiB); compact 4.10 (25.6% of BF16, 153.2 GiB); exlr8-k4 4.08 (25.5% of BF16, 152.2 GiB); k325-fp8 3.55 (22.2% of BF16, 132.7 GiB). At BF16 the same weights are 597.5 GiB. The routed experts are 94.9% of the weights and sit at 4.00 to 4.01 bits in the four configurations with K4 experts, so their whole-model figures lie close together; k325-fp8 is the one that changes the experts (3.26 bits, three quarters of the expert matrices at 3 bits and one quarter at 4). Outside the routed experts the figures spread: anchor 16.00, hqa 9.66, compact 7.25, exlr8-k4 6.55, k325-fp8 13.65. hqa to compact moves 0.67% of the weights (o_proj and q_b_proj of the main layers) from 16 bits to 6, 2.6 GiB of files, 0.1 GiB of it the same two projections in the multi-token-prediction block; anchor to compact moves {pct(mv_ac)}, 9.1 GiB. hqa and compact are one checkpoint that stores those two projections twice; each row counts the copy its setting loads. Bits per weight is a size, not a quality score: among the four measured configurations neither distance from BF16 (CP-bf16-distance) nor task score follows it. As stored is not as run: under the engine's defaults the load line of k325-fp8 reports its attention group held as FP8, converted at load, and an FP8 output head, so part of what its files hold at BF16 runs at FP8; an as-run figure is not computed because the logs do not itemize the conversion by matrix. k325-fp8 is a fifth configuration added on 2026-11-12 (protocol/AMENDMENT-2026-11-12.md); this entry holds its file accounting only, and its task passes and BF16-reference capture were running when this was written. Limits: file accounting, not memory in use and not arithmetic precision at run time; the vision tower is not counted (every configuration ran with vision off); whether the engine uses the multi-token-prediction block when serving was not checked.
